name: Ijiraq (Mythic)
body:
MYTHIC IJIRAQ
CR 11/MR 4

Its head the skull of a caribou, this humanoid has wicked claws, and wears wrappings of ragged fur adorned with scrimshaw talismans.

XP 6,400
CN Medium fey (mythic, shapechanger)
Init +3/–17; dual initiative; Senses low-light vision; Perception +21

DEFENSE

AC 31, touch 15, flat-footed 26 (+3 Dex, +2 dodge, +16 natural)
hp 129 (14d6+80)
Fort +8, Ref +14, Will +13
Defensive Abilities blurred form; DR 10/epic

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee 2 claws +10 (2d4+3), bite +10 (2d6+3), gore +10 (2d6+3)
Ranged javelin +10 (1d6+3)
Special Attacks banish into shadows, disorienting gaze, mythic power (4/day, surge +1d8)
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 14th; concentration +21)

At will—dimension door, fly, hallucinatory terrain (DC 21)
3/day—baleful polymorph (DC 22), control winds, cure critical wounds (DC 21), ice storm (DC 21), sleet storm (DC 20), summon nature’s ally IV

STATISTICS

Str 16, Dex 17, Con 18, Int 15, Wis 19, Cha 24
Base Atk +7; CMB +10; CMD 24
Feats Acrobatic Steps, Blind-Fight, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Lightning Reflexes, Mobility, Nimble Moves
Skills Escape Artist +20, Handle Animal +21, Intimidate +21, Knowledge (arcana) +16, Knowledge (nature) +19, Perception +21, Stealth +20, Survival +18
SQ change shape (any animal or magical beast native to cold forests or plains, beast shape IV), hide in plain sight

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Banish into Shadows (Su)

As a standard action, a mythic ijiraq can expend one use of mythic power and touch a single humanoid creature that is currently under the effects of its disorienting gaze in order to banish that creature to the Plane of Shadow. The creature must succeed on a Will save (DC 24) or be transported to the Plane of Shadow as though by the spell plane shift (arriving 5d100 miles away from the corresponding location on the Plane of Shadow).

The creature can return to the Material Plane if it is able to navigate its way through the Plane of Shadow to the location corresponding with where it was on the Material Plane when it was transported, but only if it can do so within 24 hours of arriving on the Plane of Shadow. A creature that realizes that it has travelled to another plane can intuitively realize where it needs to go to return, but only if it succeeds on a DC 15 Wisdom check. Creatures that fail to return in this way can still return to the Material Plane through other means.

Blurred Form (Sp)

A mythic ijiraq’s body is constantly surrounded by a faint distortion in the air, making its features indistinct and difficult to make out. This grants the mythic ijiraq concealment (20% miss chance). In conditions where the mythic ijiraq would already have concealment, or during any round when it uses the withdraw action, it gains total concealment until the end of its turn or until it moves out of the area providing concealment. A mythic ijiraq can suppress or resume this ability as a move action.

Disorienting Gaze (Su)

A mythic ijiraq can level an icy stare at a creature within 30 feet. That creature takes a –20 penalty on Perception checks and Survival checks and becomes shaken for 24 hours (Fortitude DC 24 negates). If the creature fails its saving throw by 5 or more, it is also staggered and confused for 1d4 rounds. The save DC is Charisma-based. A mythic ijiraq can use this ability while in the shape of an elk.

Hide in Plain Sight (Su)

A mythic ijiraq can use the Stealth skill even while being observed. As long as it’s standing in terrain covered in ice or snow, a mythic ijiraq can hide itself from view in the open without actually hiding behind anything. A mythic ijiraq can’t use this ability while flying, and the ability has no effect when the mythic ijiraq isn’t in icy terrain.

ECOLOGY

Environment cold forests or plains
Organization solitary
Treasure standard (mostly valuable scrimshaw carvings)

Wardens of the north, ijiraqs protect the frigid beauty and placidity of their arctic homes against all who would trespass, regardless of their intentions. Aloof and mysterious, they prefer not to be seen in their natural form, instead cloaking themselves in the fur and shape of swift elk or caribou. Yet even then they’re usually only glimpsed as fleeting shadows. Those who lock gazes with ijiraqs see the world around them begin to swim, seeming unreal to the extent that skilled foresters might lose their bearings and become lost within sight of home.

Few can honestly claim to have ever seen an ijiraq’s true face, as the creatures wear skulls taken from impressive specimens of their alternate forms as masks. Ijiraqs are 5 feet tall—plus another foot of impressive antlers—and weigh approximately 175 pounds.
